title: Teachers and Lecturers: How to Lose Weight Around School Schedules, the Canteen and Work You Bring Home
intro: Teachers' and lecturers' schedules are really packed, but you can still lose weight without a strict diet. The key is planning around your break times, the canteen and night work that's already part of your routine.

sections.p: A teacher's morning starts early and sometimes there's no time to eat. When you're very hungry, you end up eating a lot at break time. Prepare a simple breakfast like bread with eggs, or oats with milk, that you can eat in 5 minutes.
Nasi lemak is fine, ask for half rice and add an egg. Mihun soup, mee soup or rice with chicken and vegetables are also good choices. For drinks, ask for less sweet or bring your own water bottle.

sections.h: Staff room kuih and class parties
sections.p: There's always kuih in the staff room and class parties come every month. No need to refuse everything. Pick one you really want, and don't eat just because it's right in front of you.

sections.h: Work you bring home at night
sections.p: Marking books or making slides at night often comes with snacks. Prepare pre-portioned snacks, for example fruit, a handful of nuts or yogurt. Avoid eating straight from a big packet while working.

Teachers actually stand and walk a lot, that's an advantage. Walk between classes, use the stairs, and walk around the class while teaching. Lecturers who sit a lot can get up every hour for a short walk.

action: Prepare breakfast for 3 school days this week the night before.
At the canteen, try asking for half rice and adding a protein dish or vegetables.
Fill a small container with snacks before you start marking tonight.
Bring a big water bottle to school and finish it before you go home.
Do 2 short 20-minute home workouts on days with less co-curricular activity.
myth: Many think teachers who stand all day will easily slim down. Movement helps, but food still plays a big role, especially break-time meals and night snacks.

faq.q: I don't have time to exercise after school, what can I do?
faq.a: Even 15-20 minutes of exercise at home is useful, for example squats, lunges and wall push-ups. Days with co-curricular or field activities can count as active days.

faq.q: Lecturers sit in front of the computer a lot, what can we do?
faq.a: Get up every 45-60 minutes to walk, refill your water or take the stairs. If possible, hold a class or discussion standing up once in a while.

faq.q: Exam week is stressful and I eat a lot. Is that normal?
faq.a: Very normal. During this time, focus on the basics only: breakfast, water and enough sleep. Prepare light snacks so that when you're stressed, the options around you are better.
